decisions.reason: The water phantom is an early-stage option with unresolved particle therapy demand and low continuation cost, and its planned Q1/2019 US release may resolve uncertainty, so management keeps it open.
As a newly launched small volume ionization chamber, its market prospects are still uncertain but keeping it costs little, so it is retained as an option.
This second small volume ionization chamber is also an early option with unresolved value and low carrying cost, so management keeps it on the market.
The standard clinical ionization chamber is a recent launch with no negative signals and low continuation cost, so it is kept as an open option.
This relative dosimetry chamber is still in an early phase of uncertainty with minimal cost to keep, so management holds the option.
The thimble ionization chamber is a young product with uncertain demand and low keeping cost, so it is retained as an option.
